newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.10 pct in Aug 24-Sept 23.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.10 pct in Aug 24-Sept 23.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 0.10 percent in the Aug 24-Sept 23 period, down an edge from 0.11 in the previous four-week period, a Fipe official said.
Juarez Rizzieri, the president of Fipe, said a decline in food and clothing prices led the slowdown in the price index, which measures prices in the Sao Paulo area.
Food prices dropped 0.65 percent while clothing fell 2.03 percent. The period also saw slight declines in prices for transportation and education.
Rizzieri estimated September inflation could be close to zero if the slowing trend continues, he said.
He released the following breakdown of the weighted Fipe inflation index for the four-week period ended Sept 23:
-Personal expenses: 0.73 pct rise in the period
-Health care: 0.47 pct rise in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
